icons.confirmed_mapping: Pine #41 is water 2 / sun 5 / temperature 3, winter, uses lungs + wound -- and the PDF holds exactly 2 droplets, 5 suns, 3 thermometers, a snowflake, a lungs disc and a bandage disc.

review_flags.reason: No sourced water/sun/temperature values, so no droplet, sun or thermometer icons are drawn. The printed deck counts these off its own artwork; for a generated species they need a horticultural source. The icons exist and are ready.
No sourced value. GBIF occurrence counts are the obvious basis; the mapping from a count to Common/Uncommon/Rare/Epic is a product decision nobody has made.
Chamomile is a summer species, but only the WINTER snowflake has been extracted. The spring/summer/autumn icons are missing.

Only `wound` is drawn, and that is my mapping of the approved skin-support claim. The icons for digestive, calm and tea -- which the claims arguably support -- have not been extracted. Card 46, the Icon Cheat Sheet, would supply all twelve in one file.
A taste note is an observation by somebody holding the plant, not a citation. Blank.

One claim refused: the sesquiterpenoid list (chamazulene, alpha-bisabolol) was drafted at laboratory standing but its source sits in the documented-use query group, which can only support traditional. Probably true; the rule still refuses it.

The hero is a GrabCut cut-out and keeps a small artefact of stem at the upper right. No learned matte was used: a classical cut fails visibly, where a model can invent a plausible edge that is not the plant's.

publish_blockers: no cited source has been verified by a human
